decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach: orient both grippers downward gradually, right toward green and left toward red; positions estimated from head RGB.
Reduce translation and wrist rotation after initial IK continuity rejection; keep both open and preserve elbow configuration.
Continue smooth downward orientation and approach blue with right, red with left; will relocate blue to a shared centerline stacking location.
Move closer above blue and red while finishing most of the top-down wrist rotation, retaining elbow-up continuity.
Finish top-down alignment above red and blue. Blue will be moved to a central location accessible without crossing arms.
Replan from interrupted poses with smaller joint-continuous increments, completing vertical grasps above the blocks.
Refine lateral alignment from wrist RGB and descend slightly toward grasp height; avoid closing until blocks are centered.
Lower open grippers around red and blue, making small fore-aft corrections based on wrist views.
Close around red and blue at current contact-limited height, then lift gently to verify retention visually.
Lift red and blue clear of the table with closed grippers and check for stable attachment before transporting.
Blue is retained; carry it inward at safe height. Red slipped, so reopen the left gripper and correct its fore-aft grasp alignment.
Continue carrying blue toward the center with closed right gripper; descend the open left gripper to regrasp red.
Lower retained blue toward the table at an inward right-workspace base location. Recenter and close left gripper on red.
Release blue onto the table and clear it vertically. Finish closing on red, then lift to verify a secure grasp.
Blue is on the table. Red did not lift: reopen, align to its rotated faces and adjust grasp. Move right toward green overhead.
Fine-align left jaws to red's faces and approach green with right; use open jaws and limited descent.
Close left on the now face-aligned red block; finish centering right over green at grasp height.
Allow red grasp to settle and test lift. Green shifted during approach, so raise the open right gripper before recentering to avoid pushing it again.
Red now appears between the jaws; lift and begin moving inward. Recenter right above shifted green at raised clearance.
Red slipped during lift; reapproach with corrected fore-aft offset for the rotated gripper. Center green using wrist image before final vertical descent.
Descend nearly vertically around both blocks, applying small wrist-view centering corrections. Keep jaws open until at grasp depth.
Center the blocks deeper between the jaws, close fully, and dwell without lifting to establish both grasps.
Maintain fully closed commands and perform a slow vertical test lift of red and green, watching for retention rather than relying on gripper state.
Neither test lift retained a block. Reopen and shift the grasp line backward in each wrist view so the cube centers lie within the fingers, not beyond their ends.
Use smaller increments after continuity rejection; move both open grasp centers backward relative to the blocks while lowering carefully.
Reorient open jaws to match the blocks' newly rotated faces, with a small upward clearance before another deeper grasp.
Try a deeper vertical grasp with both blocks centered; stop lateral motion and close only after descending.
Dwell fully closed at the deeper grasp and make a minimal test lift to check whether either block is retained.
Lift vertically with closed jaws to assess whether the deeper grasps retain red and green.
Both blocks remain on table. Correct a likely fore-aft grasp-offset error by shifting open jaws backward at clearance, rather than repeating the same failed grasp.
Lower vertically at corrected fore-aft alignment, keeping both blocks centered between open fingers.
Close and dwell at the corrected rearward grasp line; blocks now lie farther within the open-finger region.
Test a controlled vertical lift with both grippers fully closed; verify the corrected grasps keep blocks fixed relative to the jaws.
Both blocks are visibly retained. Lift and transport inward: green toward blue, red held separately in the left workspace.
Carry green inward above table clearance. Bring retained red to the left side of a central staging area while keeping arms separated.
Approach blue with green at clearance. Lower red toward a central left-side staging spot for a later right-arm pickup without crossing arms.
Align green above blue while beginning its descent. Set red down at the central left boundary, maintaining separated approach paths.
Release staged red and retract left away from the center. Lower aligned green onto blue and open right at the expected support height.
Withdraw both open grippers from released blocks. Lift right vertically to verify the blue-green stack and begin returning left toward origin.
Blue-green stack appears stable. Red shifted left while opening, so reapproach it with left for accurate central staging; move right aside safely.
Center left above red using wrist RGB and restore the previously successful jaw orientation; keep right clear of the stack.
Lower left around the staged red block with a small lateral centering correction; right remains safely parked.
Make a final left-jaw centering adjustment at grasp height and close on red; keep the existing blue-green stack untouched.
Correct invalid row; no prior motion occurred. Lift red vertically with the left gripper closed while right remains stationary.
Move retained red to the left side of the center boundary at clearance; keep right parked away from the transfer area.
Lower red vertically to the table at the boundary staging point, keeping its pose fixed and right arm clear.
Release red without lateral motion and dwell for the fingers to open, then begin a purely vertical withdrawal to avoid dragging the block.
Lift left straight clear of released red. Bring right rearward at safe separation, matching the red pickup orientation.
Withdraw left into its own workspace while right approaches staged red from above, maintaining arm separation and stack clearance.
Right centers over red at the workspace boundary and begins descent. Left retracts toward its origin with gradual wrist restoration.
Descend right vertically around staged red without crossing the centerline; continue smooth left-arm return toward origin.
Close right around centered red and dwell at grasp depth. Continue returning left near its original position and orientation.
Lift red vertically to verify right-hand retention. Finish left-arm orientation restoration near its original pose.
Red is retained in the right gripper. Raise and carry it toward the blue-green stack with clearance; leave left at origin.
Translate retained red over the blue-green stack at clearance, then inspect alignment before lowering.
Lower red toward green with a small wrist-view lateral correction; keep the grasp closed until the final placement height.
Finish the short vertical descent and release red onto green without lateral motion; left remains at origin.
Dwell open to let red settle, then withdraw right vertically without dragging the top block.
All three blocks appear stacked. Raise right fully clear before withdrawing outward and returning it to origin.
Return right outward and rearward away from the stable stack, gradually restoring its original wrist orientation and correcting minor left-origin drift.
Reduce return-motion increments after IK continuity rejection; preserve elbow-up configuration while retreating from the stack.
Continue joint-continuous right-arm return toward its original pose, keeping the open gripper away from the completed stack.
Continue restoring right-arm origin pose smoothly; the blue-green-red stack remains undisturbed.
Approach right origin with small synchronized translation and wrist restoration, maintaining open grippers and configuration continuity.
Complete the final gradual right-arm return to its original pose; keep both grippers open and the blue-green-red stack untouched.
